summary: Wabeno was one of six Prince Albert National Park fire towers; the museum says the park's towers were decommissioned in 2001 and replaced by helicopter patrols.

facts.status_note: The museum says the park's fire towers were decommissioned in 2001; no source describes the Wabeno tower itself today.

events.note: Inferred from list order: the museum dates the first five of its six towers to 1938, and Wabeno is third of six on its list, so among the first five if the list follows build order; not stated for Wabeno directly
Park fire towers decommissioned and replaced by helicopter smoke patrols, per the museum; Wabeno is one of the park's towers

notes_for_editor: The 1938 build year is inferred: the museum says 'The first 5 were constructed in 1938' and gives Boundary as 1940, and it lists Wabeno third of six names (Blue Bell, Summit, Wabeno, Sanctuary, Rabbit Creek, Boundary), so Wabeno falls among the first five only if the list follows build order; the museum does not name the five directly, so check before using 1938 as fact. The decommissioning date conflicts with a UER forum thread that a search snippet puts at the 1990s ('decommissioned all 7 of their towers ... in the 90's'); that thread returned 403 to the fetch tool, so it is not cited and needs a manual check. The websiteservice Wabeno coordinates match the brief; the 'WABENO TOWER' park entry has no location of its own, so linking the two rests on the shared name. Park-wide staffing and design details come from the museum's general description, not from Wabeno-specific records. Access is left unset because no source says whether the park tower sites are open. The brief's status 'unknown' was changed to 'decommissioned' in facts because the museum's park-wide statement covers Wabeno; the editor may want to soften this to a note. No photos found.
